tagline: US 60 links Lexington’s urban service boundary with the Clark County line
intro: Winchester Road Corridor follows US 60 for 4.8 miles between Lexington’s Urban Service Area boundary and the Clark County line. The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet lists it as a scenic route designated on February 24, 2011.

That starting point has a planning history: Lexington established its urban growth boundary in 1958, restricting new development to an urban service area. Fayette Alliance describes the boundary as a way to protect farmland and limit the cost of extending city services. In 2000, Lexington adopted a program to purchase development rights from existing farms. The designated drive follows US 60 from the urban service boundary to the county line.

moments.title: The urban service boundary
moments.text: The state’s designation begins at Lexington’s Urban Service Area boundary. Lexington adopted its urban growth boundary in 1958. Fayette Alliance describes the boundary as protecting farmland from development.

moments.title: Along US 60
moments.text: The scenic corridor follows US Highway 60 through Fayette County between the urban service boundary and Clark County. The state’s recorded length is 4.8 miles.

moments.title: Clark County line
moments.text: The Clark County line marks the other end of the Winchester Road Corridor’s 2011 scenic designation.
